title: PI information organization: project groups, people-edges, and portfolio views
description: A PI deploys Lab Tracker with many projects and project-scoped trainees. Today there is no container above Project, no real notion of people (created_by is a free string; the only cross-project tier is global ADMIN), and oversight requires being a global admin. This epic adds an organizing-edge layer — a Lab/project-group container, supervision and ownership edges, and read-only portfolio/lab-health views — without becoming an identity provider, HR system, or grants-management product. Build-vs-buy moat preserved: identity stays offloadable; we own the semantic edges.
design:
CONCEPT: Add the three semantic edges no identity provider models — group ownership, supervision, attribution — onto the existing model; route PI oversight through accessible_project_ids(). No org-chart/HR/IdP/grants-management.

NEW: project_groups (kind=lab) + group_memberships (reuse VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR/OWNER enum); supervision_edges (dated, own table keyed by user_id, NOT a users column); shadow FK created_by_user_id/executed_by_user_id (additive; string stays, dual-written).
CHANGE: goals.project_id nullable + GoalLink EntityType.PROJECT slot (enum value already exists, models.py:155); accessible_project_ids()/membership_role() group-aware.
REUSE: prov:Agent -> prov:Person/wasAttributedTo/actedOnBehalfOf (export-only); project_graph, decision_context (stays single-project), graph-draft human review, goals.

ACCESS CONTRACT (2.1, asymmetric): group OWNER inherits OWNER on every child project (PI oversight w/o global admin); group VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR inherit NOTHING unless an explicit per-group group_read_all flag (default false). Direct project membership resolves first; admin short-circuit and >=1-owner-per-project guard untouched.

BOUNDARY: every new edge points at the offloadable users table but adds NO domain column to users itself. Aggregations (portfolio/lab-health) read only over the in-house question/claim/goal graph — not a metrics/ELN dashboard.

PHASES: 0 read-only portfolio (zero schema) -> 1 group container + group-aware access -> 2 attribution FK (isolated) -> 3 spanning goals + supervision + PROV-O people -> 4 offboarding export + ownership reassignment. Each additive, single Alembic head.

Source: multi-agent design pass (2026-06-15), grounded in db_models.py, services/project_authorization.py, auth.py, provenance.py, docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md, docs/retained-v1-surface.md.

title: Build-vs-buy: define Lab Tracker responsibility boundaries vs existing tools
description: Lab Tracker's durable product is the PROV-O / JSON-LD semantic provenance spine threading questions -> notes -> sessions -> datasets -> analyses -> claims -> visualizations (see src/lab_tracker/provenance.py). It is anchored by two node types no external tool provides: Questions (broad-to-atomic inquiry structure) and Claims (epistemic layer linking evidence to conclusions with confidence). Many adjacent responsibilities are either commodity infrastructure or owned by mature tool categories that Lab Tracker risks accidentally half-reimplementing: identity/RBAC, byte/asset storage, data versioning, experiment tracking, note capture (ELNs), transcription, and search. This epic decomposes the boundary decisions: for each adjacent responsibility decide offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house, so effort concentrates on the irreducible semantic core. Already-resolved boundaries: voice transcription is offloaded to an explicit note-scoped action (retained-v1); multimodal note-to-graph extraction is offloaded to the LLM while the human-gated draft->commit diff stays in-house; semantic/vector search is explicitly deferred in retained-v1.
design: Shared principle - pointer-not-reimplementation: for each adjacent responsibility, store a reference (URI + content hash) to the external tool's artifact PLUS the semantic edges the external tool does not model (which question a dataset addresses, which claim an analysis supports). Do not reimplement the external tool's core. The PROV-O export is the integration seam: ingest external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities and connect them to inquiry and claims. Integrate decisions should strengthen the core by letting it focus on the semantic graph, not shrink it. Danger zone: each integrate decision is a slippery slope toward rebuilding half of MLflow or half of an ELN - resist field-by-field creep past a reference + edges.
acceptance_criteria: Each child decision reaches a recorded outcome (offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house / defer) with rationale, a concrete integration seam or boundary description, and follow-up implementation issues filed where needed. The retained-v1 surface doc (docs/retained-v1-surface.md) and architecture notes are updated to reflect chosen boundaries. Tool-landscape names are validated as current before committing to any one.
close_reason: Completed build-vs-buy boundary epic: all six child decisions recorded and closed, follow-up adapter/storage issues filed, retained-v1 and internal boundary docs updated, PROV-O ingestion seam implemented with dataset external-artifact round-trip coverage, pytest and Ruff passed.

title: Make request lifecycle context-managed
description: Replace finish_request(committed=...) and middleware-level mutable commit flags with a context-managed request lifecycle. The current caller must remember whether a database session committed before deferred after-commit or after-rollback hooks run, which is easy to misuse on exception or rollback paths.
design: Introduce a request-scope/context-manager API that owns repository binding, commit/rollback outcome, deferred-action dispatch, and cleanup. The FastAPI database middleware should enter the request scope, run the handler, commit or roll back through one explicit lifecycle path, and let the scope fire after_commit only after a successful commit and after_rollback only on rollback/error. Keep public route and LabTrackerAPI behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: finish_request(committed=...) is removed or reduced to a non-public compatibility shim that no caller must use. Middleware no longer tracks a mutable committed flag to decide deferred hooks. after_commit hooks run only after a successful commit; after_rollback hooks run on rollback/error paths. Route/session tests cover successful commit and rollback/error behavior. Backend tests pass.

title: Epic: Lab Tracker consumer integration toolkit
description:
Coordinate the Lab Tracker consumer integration toolkit so downstream repos can capture project/question/note context without each repo maintaining brittle scripts, MCP config, and skill prose.

Filed from the LiteratureEmbeddings repo after back-filling Lab Tracker integration end-to-end on 2026-05-26/27. A consumer repo that wants to track work in Lab Tracker currently has to reinvent four pieces of plumbing: HTTP client, idempotent upsert pattern, MCP wiring, and API-shape guidance generated by reading /openapi.json. The current external lab-tracker skill prose has drifted from the live API, e.g. it describes question fields/enums such as title/broad/atomic while the API expects text and descriptive | hypothesis_driven | method_dev | other.

title: Design and implement dry-run record_evidence_bundle MCP tool
description: Authoring one research result through MCP still requires multiple ID-dependent calls across questions, datasets, analyses, claims, visualizations, and optional source notes. Design and implement an additive composite tool that previews and then creates an evidence bundle while preserving Lab Tracker's strict endpoints and provenance boundaries.
design: Add a record_evidence_bundle surface with dry_run defaulting true, explicit idempotency/natural-key behavior, and no silent over-commit. Split provenance by node type: datasets use content-addressed commit manifests from uploaded/resolved artifacts or supplied manifests; repo-derived provenance applies to analyses/code versions through a resolve_code_provenance primitive. Handle locality explicitly: if the MCP client sees a local artifact path but the API server may not, upload or resolve through MCP rather than assuming the server can read the path. Keep strict create endpoints unchanged and route final writes through existing API validation.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run returns a fully reviewable plan including proposed nodes, links, reused records, warnings, and derived provenance values when derivation is possible. Calling with dry_run=false creates or reuses the expected records through existing API paths and returns stable IDs. Re-running with the same idempotency key or natural keys does not create duplicates. Dirty repo state and unreadable/local-only artifacts produce explicit warnings or errors, not fabricated hashes. Tests cover dry-run, commit, idempotent retry, dataset manifest provenance, analysis code provenance, visualization upload/path handling, and backward compatibility of existing MCP create tools. Ruff and relevant backend/MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added dry-run/idempotent MCP evidence bundle planner and executor through strict API endpoints

title: Make decision-context MCP output a write-friendly front door

design: Keep the tool read-only. Preserve existing research task_kind values such as plot, analysis, slides, experiment_plan, summary, and research_writing; do not mix them with workflow intents like log_result unless a separate workflow_intent field is introduced. Echo resolved project scope, anchors, candidate IDs, allowed task kinds, and concise guidance for subsequent creates. Coordinate with the schema metadata bead so vocabulary is defined once.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP tool description clearly says to call decision context first for research-facing read-then-write tasks. Responses include enough stable IDs and candidate entities to support subsequent create calls without avoidable project/question/dataset lookups. Existing API response shape stays backward-compatible or changes are additive. Tests cover allowed task_kind reporting and ID echo behavior. Ruff and relevant decision-context/MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added write-front-door decision-context metadata and MCP call-first guidance

title: Expose MCP schema metadata and enum affordances
description: MCP tools currently expose many controlled values as unconstrained strings, so agents have to infer task_kind, question_type, statuses, goal relations, and link statuses from prose or failed calls. Add a discoverable schema/metadata surface and improve MCP tool schemas/descriptions so agents can see allowed values and status lifecycles at the point of use.
design: Generate schema metadata from the existing source of truth: Pydantic request models, lab_tracker.models enums, decision_context_constants.TASK_KIND_VALUES, and service status-transition maps. Treat viz_type separately as a free-string convention unless a later product decision makes it an enum. Prefer a lab_tracker_describe_schema MCP/API surface plus tighter FastMCP argument metadata where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Agents can discover allowed task_kind values, entity statuses, question/session/goal enums, goal relation/link-status values, required fields, and known lifecycle transitions without reading source. The generated metadata is tested against model constants so it cannot drift silently. Existing create/list tools remain backward-compatible. Ruff and relevant MCP tests pass.
close_reason: Added source-derived schema metadata discovery via API and MCP, with enum/lifecycle tests

title: MCP agent write ergonomics for Lab Tracker
description: Track additive MCP improvements from the 2026-06-12 Lab-Tracker MCP Agent Ergonomics Proposal rev 2. Goal: make agents reach Lab Tracker for research-context writes by default while preserving retained-v1 schema, API validation, human-gated graph changes, and manifest/code provenance boundaries.
design: Sequence low-risk schema and tool-description changes before composite authoring. Do not overload sessions; sessions remain acquisition activity. Dataset hashes remain content-addressed manifests. Repo-derived provenance applies only to analyses and code versions. viz_type remains a free string unless a separate product decision standardizes it.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads cover schema/enum discovery, decision-context front-door affordances, and a dry-run/idempotent record_evidence_bundle design. Existing strict create endpoints remain backward-compatible. Retained v1 boundaries are unchanged.

title: Planned-figure specs: promote goal figure_slot from string to structured FigureSpec with origin provenance
description: Goals can be specified before their data/analysis exist — a PI sketches 'plot firing rate vs contrast as Figure 3' on a whiteboard during a lab meeting, months before the recording session or analysis. Today a paper goal's planned figures are bare strings (PaperAttributes.figure_slots: list[str] in goals_attributes.py) and a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink can only target an already-rendered Visualization entity (which requires analysis_id + file_path). So two things go unrecorded: (1) the INTENT of a planned figure — what is meant to be plotted, against what, to answer which question/claim; and (2) the MECHANISM of its specification — which note/session/whiteboard-asset it originated from, when, and via what medium. This promotes the planned-figure slot from a string to a structured, machine-readable FigureSpec carrying intent + origin provenance, WITHOUT inventing a new entity or table. Follow-on to lab-tracker-co0 (closed).
design: Add a FigureSpec Pydantic model in goals_attributes.py (extra='forbid') and change PaperAttributes.figure_slots from list[str] to list[FigureSpec]. FigureSpec fields: slot (str, required label e.g. 'Figure 3'); intent — x (str|None), y (str|None), grouping (str|None), plot_kind (str|None e.g. scatter/line/bar), comparison (str|None free-text 'this against that'); semantic edges — target_question_id (UUID|None), target_claim_id (UUID|None); origin provenance — origin (EntityRef|None pointing at the note/session/whiteboard-asset), specified_at (date|None), medium (str|None e.g. 'whiteboard','lab_meeting'). Lives in the validated attributes JSON blob — NO schema migration, NO new table. Realization path stays complementary, not duplicated: when a real Visualization is later created, a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink with slot == FigureSpec.slot links it and candidate->committed marks the slot filled; FigureSpec describes the PLAN, GoalLink records FULFILLMENT. Backward compat: accept legacy list[str] on read and coerce each string s to FigureSpec(slot=s); stored-JSON migration is lazy (on next write). Wire through goals_attributes validation, schemas.py goal create/update payloads, the MCP write tool (suggest_new_goal / update_goal already exist), and the IMAGE_ONLY graph-draft path so a whiteboard photo -> Note.raw_asset -> suggested goal can auto-populate FigureSpec.origin. Boundary: this is the LIGHTWEIGHT option chosen over a first-class PlannedVisualization entity precisely to avoid scope creep — it must stay a thin semantic-metadata layer and NOT become a slot-coverage board, figure-layout editor, or plotting tool (docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md).
acceptance_criteria: A paper goal stores figure_slots as structured FigureSpec objects (x/y/plot_kind/comparison + target_question_id/target_claim_id + origin EntityRef), validated with extra='forbid'. Legacy list[str] figure_slots still validate and round-trip (coerced to FigureSpec(slot=s)). A FigureSpec can be created with an origin note/session BEFORE any Visualization or Analysis exists. Invalid/unknown fields are rejected. Tests in tests/test_goals.py cover: structured create, legacy-string coercion, invalid-field rejection, and origin EntityRef round-trip. No new table or migration; change confined to the attributes blob. Stays within the build-vs-buy boundary (documented).
notes: Existing hooks to reuse: GraphDraftMode.IMAGE_ONLY, GraphDraftSemanticType.SUGGEST_NEW_GOAL / LINK_NODE_TO_GOAL, Note.raw_asset (whiteboard photo), GoalRelation.CANDIDATE_FIGURE, GoalLink.slot, GoalLinkStatus.candidate/committed. Heavier alternative (deferred): a first-class PlannedVisualization entity that CANDIDATE_FIGURE can target before any Analysis exists and that is later realized into a Visualization — revisit only if repeated need proves it.

title: Goals/outputs: flexible goal entity + node-tagging on the provenance spine
description:
The PI wants Lab Tracker to represent GOALS (aspirational research outputs: papers, grants, talks) and let existing graph nodes (questions, claims, datasets, analyses, visualizations) be tagged 'in relation to' a goal output (e.g. 'this figure is a candidate for Figure 3 of paper X', 'this claim addresses Aim 2 of grant Y'). The relation is often tentative ('possible'), and goal types are heterogeneous, so the representation must be flexible.

Chosen design (from a multi-approach design review): a first-class project-scoped 'goals' table with a validated JSON 'attributes' blob, plus a polymorphic 'goal_links' tag table modeled on NoteTargetModel and carrying a relation + link_status pair like dataset_question_links. Flexibility comes from a per-goal-type Pydantic registry over the JSON attributes (extra='forbid' per type + an 'other' escape hatch), NOT per-type subtables. Goals are a new EntityType node in the graph; creating a goal is direct CRUD, while tagging a node to a goal rides the human-gated GraphChangeSet spine.

v1 decisions: goal types = paper, grant, talk (+ 'other' escape hatch; thesis_chapter/patent are trivial later additions). goal_links uses a synthetic link_id PK so a node can hold multiple relations/slots per goal.

Build-vs-buy guardrail: stays a thin semantic layer on the PROV-O reasoning spine (pointers + edges + light metadata). It must NOT grow into a manuscript editor / reference manager / grants-management or slot-coverage board; that is the line recorded in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md.
design: Base approach: json-attrs-entity. Tables: goals (goal_id PK, project_id CASCADE FK, goal_type, title, summary Text, status, target_date Date, external_ref String(1000), attributes sa.JSON, created_by, created_at/updated_at; index on project_id,created_at) and goal_links (link_id String(36) PK, goal_id CASCADE FK, entity_type String(30), entity_id String(36), relation String(40), link_status String(20) default candidate, slot String(120) nullable, created_by, created_at; UNIQUE(goal_id,entity_type,entity_id,relation,slot); index ix_goal_links_entity_lookup on entity_type,entity_id,goal_id mirroring ix_note_targets_entity_lookup; index on goal_id,link_status). Enums: GoalType(paper,grant,talk,other), GoalStatus(planned,in_progress,submitted,accepted,abandoned), GoalRelation(contributes_to,addresses,candidate_figure,supporting_evidence,background,methods), GoalLinkStatus(candidate,committed,dropped). EntityType gains GOAL. JSON columns are plain sa.JSON() per repo convention (no JSONB in this codebase). Single alembic head confirmed = 0021_claim_questions (down_revision for new migration 0022).
notes: Source: design workflow synthesis (5 approaches, 4 adversarial lens-judges). Verified against live code: single alembic head 0021_claim_questions; _CREATE_SCHEMAS/_UPDATE_SCHEMAS/_SEMANTIC_ALLOWED_TARGETS dispatch maps in services/graph_draft_validation.py; LINK_NOTE_TO_* family modeled as (UPDATE, NOTE) so there is no generic link primitive (a goal UPDATE applier branch is required); JSON columns use sa.JSON() not JSONB.
close_reason: Completed flexible goals entity, node tagging, API/MCP, graph/frontend, and graph-draft integration.

2026-05-28 representation decision for retained-v1:

Keep the three explicit representations for now. Domain models remain the service/repository contract and the place where retained-v1 domain fields are expressed without SQLAlchemy session behavior leaking upward. SQLAlchemy ORM models remain persistence-only database rows. Pydantic schemas remain the HTTP/MCP wire/input boundary rather than being generated from ORM models during retained-v1.

Do not collapse to SQLAlchemy-as-domain, SQLModel, or generated schemas in this phase. Those options could delete code, but they would also couple route payload shape, persistence mapping, and migration details during an active architecture cleanup. The safer tradeoff is to keep the boundary and reduce its maintenance cost.

Mapper responsibility stays explicit but should move from one monolithic sqlalchemy_mappers.py file into focused aggregate/entity modules with narrow tests and a compatibility barrel for existing imports. The pilot entity is Project: extract Project mapping into a focused mapper module, wire repository persistence through it, preserve the old import surface, and cover mapper plus project persistence/API behavior. Follow-up work should split the remaining mapper groups in the same style.

EnrollPage keeps a manual override path (?label=foo) so the user can pair multiple phones distinguishably if needed, but defaults to UA-derived label.

Given a set of staged notes, it builds the context packet, calls the configured client, persists the resulting proposal set as a pending batch with full traceability back to the source notes, and handles model failures with bounded retries + a dead-letter record so the runner can surface them.

Splits out of lab-tracker-641 once the provider abstraction and the OpenAI client method landed; persistence touches the data model (GraphChangeSet currently ties to a single source note and needs either schema extension or a sibling BatchGraphDraft entity) and warrants its own commit and review pass.

Either way, every operation in the persisted record must trace back to the note(s) that motivated it via existing source_refs. Retries: bounded (e.g. 3) with exponential backoff for transient HTTP errors; non-retryable validation failures go straight to dead-letter. Dead-letter is a persisted record with the failure category, error text, and the offending input so a human can inspect.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_batch_graph_draft(notes, *, user_hint=None, actor=None) on the service layer
- Persists a pending batch with operation-level traceability to source note ids
- Retries transient model errors with bounded attempts + backoff
- Dead-letter record on terminal failure with category, error, and input snapshot
- Tests cover: success path persistence, retry on transient error, dead-letter on terminal error, empty-batch short-circuit

The batch report is one document covering all proposed changes in the batch; tabbed navigation between proposed changes is an optional organizing device, not a requirement.

Option (b) is simpler to ship; option (a) is the long-term right answer. Pick one and document the reason.

title: Epic: Scheduled AI graph-draft batch (user-set cadence)
description:
Replace per-note draft generation with a scheduled batch at a cadence the user sets. Drafting on every upload thrashes context and wastes model calls on incomplete information; a batch cadence lets the model see accumulated notes together, dedupe, propose coherent multi-note merges, and produce a single review queue.

Goal: at the user-set cadence (daily is a sensible default, not a requirement), a scheduled agent wakes up, collects all notes that landed since the last run, builds a graph-aware context packet covering them, tries to figure out proposed graph operations (new nodes, edges, claim updates), and stores the result as a pending batch in the existing graph-draft review UI. The human reviews per batch instead of per note.

Pairs with the 'PWA capture-first phone workflow' epic: capture cheaply through the day, review proposals in one sitting.
design:
Batch is the unit of review, not the individual note. Cadence is a user-facing setting: setting or changing it (re)schedules an agent that wakes up at that cadence, reads the accumulated inputs, and tries to figure out the changes. Runner is idempotent (re-runnable on the same window without duplicates). Context builder pulls unprocessed notes + the relevant graph slice (projects/questions touched). Draft generator can propose merges across multiple notes (e.g. three photos from the same gel become one observation). Review UI extends the existing graph-draft card pattern to a batch container.

Report/review surface decisions (2026-06-10): review is expected to happen at a computer, so do NOT constrain report layout for phones (fine if it happens to render there, but never a design constraint). One report summarizes all proposed changes in a batch; tabs per proposed change (or per change category) are an acceptable way to organize it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled agent runs at the user-set cadence, idempotently, with configurable window
- Cadence is a user setting; changing it reschedules the agent
- Batch context builder collects all notes since last successful run + relevant graph slice
- Draft generator produces a structured proposal set covering the batch
- A single report/review surface summarizes all proposed changes in the batch (tabs per change optional), with per-operation accept/reject
- Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path
- Rejected/edited operations are recorded for future model feedback
- Notification surfaces when a new batch is ready for review
close_reason: Completed scheduled graph-draft batches end-to-end: user-set cadence and due/manual runner, idempotent persisted batch runs, batch proposal persistence with traceability and dead-letter metadata, Anthropic/Google providers, desktop batch review queue/detail with per-operation accept/reject/edit and model-feedback notes, and in-app ready-batch notification. Gates: pytest 320 passed; ruff check src tests scripts alembic skills passed; npm run test:frontend passed; npm run lint:frontend passed; npm run build:frontend passed.

title: Epic: PWA capture-first phone workflow

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.

Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.

- Service worker caches the app shell and queues failed uploads with retry

title: Clarify and harden MCP note creation validation for status and metadata
description:
While recording the 2026-04-28 temporal-gradient projector titration analysis through the Lab Tracker MCP connector, `lab_tracker_create_note` accepted only a reduced payload after two confusing validation failures.

Observed behavior:
- Creating a note with `status="active"` failed, while the analogous question flow accepts `active`. This is technically consistent with `NoteStatus` (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`), but the MCP tool exposes `status` as a free string and the skill/API docs do not make the note-specific allowed values obvious.
- Creating a note with structured metadata failed unless all metadata values were strings. `NoteCreate.metadata` is typed as `dict[str, str]`, so Pydantic rejects non-string JSON values before the request reaches `_normalize_note_metadata`, even though the service normalizer is written to coerce non-string values to strings.
- The successful fallback was to create the note with `status="staged"` and no metadata, which avoided data loss but made the assistant workflow more brittle and less informative.

Concrete example context:
- Project: `b97935f1-42c6-475d-b35f-0e23607d11e6`
- Successful fallback note: `4dc2ec50-7781-475d-ba3d-b89c0c79895b`
- MCP tool: `lab_tracker_create_note`
- Relevant code paths noticed during triage: `src/lab_tracker/schemas.py` (`NoteCreate.metadata: dict[str, str]`, `status: NoteStatus | None`), `src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py` (`lab_tracker_create_note(status: str | None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None)`), and `src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py` (`_normalize_note_metadata` coerces values).

Why this matters:
Assistant clients will naturally use project/question status vocabulary and structured provenance metadata. The current behavior requires hidden knowledge of note-specific status values and silently discourages preserving useful machine-readable provenance on notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lab_tracker_create_note` docs/schema expose the allowed note statuses (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`) clearly, or the MCP layer rejects invalid statuses with a targeted error before the generic API failure.
- Decide whether note metadata should accept JSON scalar values and normalize them, or remain string-only; make the API schema, service normalizer, MCP type hints, and docs agree.
- Add or update tests for MCP note creation covering invalid note status and metadata values with at least one non-string scalar.
- Update the Lab Tracker skill/docs so assistant clients know the note status vocabulary and metadata contract.
close_reason: Clarified note status validation and aligned scalar metadata handling across API, MCP, tests, docs, and installed skills.

title: Storage ops robustness - acquisition watcher and dolt mirror
description: The watcher loop dies permanently on any API/DB error (acquisition_watcher.py:85), can register a checksum/size pair from two different file states with no stability check (line 63), and skips all files under dot-named ancestor directories (line 33); failed streaming uploads leak orphan temp files (file_storage.py:150); the dolt mirror never propagates schema changes after table creation (dolt_mirror.py:119), exports without snapshot isolation (line 83), and conflates NULL with empty string in CSV (line 153). Add per-file error handling with backoff, stability checks, a relative hidden-check, temp cleanup on failure, schema-drift handling, and a REPEATABLE READ export transaction. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.

title: Decision: offload byte/asset storage to object storage

Keep a local-filesystem backend for single-workstation use behind the same interface. Relates to lab-tracker-6lx (portable visualization assets).

title: Notify when a new batch is ready for review
description:
When the scheduled batch job (runs at the user-set cadence) completes successfully and a non-empty proposal set lands, notify the user. Channel options: web push (via the PWA service worker), email, or in-app banner.

Web push is the natural pairing with the PWA work — the same service worker that handles offline capture can receive push notifications. Start with in-app banner + email; add web push once the PWA infrastructure is in place. The notification links to the batch report, which is reviewed at a computer (desktop-first; the notification itself may of course arrive on a phone).
acceptance_criteria:
- In-app banner on next app open shows pending batch count
- Optional email digest (configurable per user)
- Web push notification when PWA + push subscription are available
- Notification links directly to the batch detail view
close_reason: Implemented in-app pending-batch banner showing ready count and links to the first batch or full batch queue; web push remains channel-dependent on future PWA push infrastructure. Gates: frontend test/lint/build passed; pytest 320 passed.
